**1. ESTABLISHMENT**

1.1 The Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee (hereinafter "the Committee") is established by the Office of Product Safety (OPS) pursuant to the powers conferred under the *Product Safety (Advisory Bodies) Act 2010* (Cth) and the *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth), Schedule 2, Part 3-3.

1.2 The Committee is constituted as a non-statutory advisory body. It operates at arm's length from the OPS and reports to the Minister for Consumer Affairs.

1.3 The Committee is established on the date of execution of this Charter, being 14 March 2012. That date shall be recorded in the OPS register as the date of establishment of the Committee for all administrative and reporting purposes. The Committee's establishment date is current and shall remain so unless and until this Charter is formally revoked or replaced by a subsequent instrument.

1.4 Nothing in this Charter confers on the Committee any regulatory, enforcement, or standard-setting power. The Committee is advisory only.

**2. OBJECT AND FUNCTIONS**

2.1 The object of the Committee is to provide independent, evidence-based advice to the Minister and to OPS on matters relating to the safety of consumer products supplied in or imported into Australia.

2.2 In pursuit of that object, the Committee shall:

(a) identify and assess emerging and ongoing product safety risks;

(b) review and advise on the adequacy and effectiveness of existing product safety regulatory frameworks and voluntary industry codes;

(c) advise on priorities for product safety research, data collection, and surveillance;

(d) make recommendations on the need for, and content of, mandatory safety standards, bans, and information standards;

(e) advise on the effectiveness of product recall processes and on improvements to those processes;

(f) consider submissions and representations from consumer groups, industry bodies, and the public, where those submissions raise matters of systemic product safety concern;

(g) provide advice on international product safety developments, including standards harmonisation and the exchange of information with overseas regulators; and

(d) the need for consistency with Australia's international trade obligations; and

(e) the imperative of timely advice, particularly where a product presents an imminent and serious risk of injury.

**SCHEDULE C: MEMBERSHIP — CATEGORIES AND APPOINTMENT**

Membership of the Committee shall, to the extent practicable, reflect a balance of the following categories:

(a) persons with expertise in consumer product safety, including product design, engineering, and materials science;

(b) persons with expertise in public health, injury prevention, or epidemiology;

(c) persons with expertise in consumer affairs, including consumer advocacy;

(d) persons with expertise in product safety regulation or enforcement, including from State or Territory agencies;

(e) persons with expertise in manufacturing, supply chains, or retail; and

(f) such other persons as the Minister considers appropriate.
**10. COMMITTEE OBJECTIVES**

10.1 The principal objective of the Australian Consumer Product Safety Committee is to provide independent, evidence-based advice to the Minister on matters relating to the safety of consumer products in Australia.

10.2 In pursuing this objective, the Committee shall:

(a) identify and assess current and emerging product safety risks, including risks associated with new technologies, materials, and supply chains;

(b) evaluate the effectiveness of existing regulatory and non-regulatory measures, including mandatory and voluntary standards, bans, and recall processes;

(c) recommend priorities for product safety research, data collection, and surveillance;

(d) advise on the development, amendment, or revocation of consumer product safety standards and bans;

(e) consider international developments in product safety regulation and standards harmonisation, and advise on their implications for Australia;

(f) promote a consistent and coordinated approach to product safety across the Commonwealth, States, and Territories; and

(g) perform such other functions as the Minister may, from time to time, direct.

10.3 The Committee’s advice shall be informed by the best available evidence, including scientific research, injury data, incident reports, and input from stakeholders. Where evidence is limited or inconclusive, the Committee shall identify gaps and make recommendations for further investigation.

10.4 The Committee shall have regard to the costs and benefits of any proposed regulatory or non-regulatory measures, including the potential impacts on consumers, industry, and the community, and shall seek to avoid unnecessary regulatory burden while ensuring an appropriate level of consumer protection.

**11. STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT**

11.1 The Committee recognises that effective product safety regulation requires the active engagement of a broad range of stakeholders, including consumers, industry, government agencies, and professional bodies.

11.2 In discharging its functions, the Committee shall:

(a) establish and maintain mechanisms for consulting with consumer groups, industry associations, manufacturers, importers, retailers, and other interested parties;

(b) invite submissions from stakeholders on specific issues or proposals where appropriate;

(c) hold public forums, roundtables, or workshops as it considers necessary to inform its advice;

(d) consider submissions received and have regard to the range of views expressed in formulating its recommendations;

(e) liaise with relevant Commonwealth, State, and Territory government agencies, including those responsible for consumer affairs, health, and fair trading; and

(f) engage with international counterparts and relevant international organisations to share information and promote cooperation on product safety matters.

11.3 The Committee may establish working groups or subcommittees to engage with stakeholders on particular issues, and may co-opt additional expertise as required for specific tasks.

11.4 Stakeholders who provide submissions to the Committee may request that their submission, or any part of it, be treated as confidential. The Committee shall consider such requests and, where confidentiality is granted, shall not disclose the submission except as required by law.

11.5 The Committee shall make publicly available a summary of stakeholder engagement activities undertaken in each reporting period, including the number and type of consultations conducted, without disclosing confidential information.
**12. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

12.1 The Committee is committed to ensuring that its deliberations and recommendations are, and are seen to be, independent, impartial, and free from undue influence. Accordingly, members shall comply with the conflict of interest provisions set out in this clause and with any applicable requirements of the *Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013* (Cth) and the *Commonwealth Procurement Rules*.

12.2 For the purposes of this clause, a conflict of interest may be actual, potential, or perceived. A conflict arises where a member's personal, professional, financial, or other interests could be reasonably regarded as affecting, or appearing to affect, the member's ability to act in the best interests of the Committee and to discharge their duties objectively.

12.3 Each member shall, upon appointment and thereafter at the commencement of each financial year, complete and lodge with the Secretariat a declaration of interests in the form prescribed by the Chair. The declaration shall include:

(a) any financial interest, including shareholdings, directorships, partnerships, or other business interests, held by the member or by a member of their immediate family;

(b) any employment, consultancy, or other professional engagement undertaken by the member, whether paid or unpaid, that relates to the supply, manufacture, importation, or regulation of consumer products;

(c) any membership of, or advisory role with, any industry association, consumer organisation, professional body, or government committee whose activities may be relevant to the work of the Committee;

(d) any other matter that the member reasonably considers may give rise to a conflict of interest.

12.4 Members shall have a continuing obligation to disclose any new or changed interest as soon as practicable after the interest arises. Disclosure shall be made in writing to the Chair and to the Secretariat, and shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting of the Committee.

12.5 Where a matter before the Committee gives rise to a conflict of interest in relation to a member, that member shall:

(a) declare the nature of the conflict to the Committee prior to any discussion of the matter;

(b) not participate in any deliberation or decision in relation to the matter, unless the Committee, having considered the declaration, determines otherwise;

(c) absent themselves from the meeting during discussion and voting on the matter, unless the Committee determines otherwise; and

(d) not seek to influence, directly or indirectly, the deliberations or recommendations of the Committee in relation to the matter.

12.6 The Chair may, after consulting the member concerned, direct that a member with a conflict of interest take such further steps as are necessary to manage the conflict, including but not limited to restricting access to documents or excluding the member from certain parts of a meeting.

12.7 A member who is uncertain whether a conflict of interest exists in relation to a particular matter may raise the matter with the Chair, who shall determine the question in consultation with the member and, if necessary, with the Committee as a whole.

12.8 The register of interests shall be maintained by the Secretariat and shall be available for inspection by the Minister and, subject to any applicable privacy obligations, by other members of the Committee. The register shall not be made publicly available unless the Minister determines otherwise.
**CHARTER AND TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**AUSTRALIAN CONSUMER PRODUCT SAFETY ADVISORY COMMITTEE**

**Part 13 — Dissolution and Winding Up**

13.1 The Committee shall continue in existence until such time as the Minister, by written notice to the Chair, determines that the Committee is to be dissolved. The notice shall specify the date upon which the dissolution takes effect and any transitional arrangements that the Minister considers necessary or desirable.

13.2 Upon receipt of a notice of dissolution, the Chair shall, as soon as practicable, convene a meeting of the Committee for the purpose of:

(a) considering the notice and any transitional arrangements specified therein;

(b) preparing a final report to the Minister on the work of the Committee, including any outstanding recommendations or matters of concern;

(c) determining the arrangements for the custody and disposal of the records of the Committee, including minutes, reports, correspondence, and the register of interests; and

(d) considering any other matter arising from the dissolution.

13.3 The final report referred to in clause 13.2(b) shall be submitted to the Minister within 60 days of the date of dissolution, unless the Minister directs otherwise in writing.

13.4 The Secretariat shall, upon dissolution, transfer all records of the Committee to the Minister or to such other person or body as the Minister may direct. Records that are identified as having ongoing administrative value shall be retained in accordance with the Archives Act 1983 (Cth) and any other applicable record-keeping obligations.

13.5 Where a matter before the Committee is incomplete at the date of dissolution, the Chair shall include in the final report a summary of the matter, the progress made to date, and any recommendations for further action by the Minister or by any other body.

13.6 Nothing in this Part prevents the Minister from establishing a new committee with similar or related functions following the dissolution of the Committee, whether under the same name or under a different name.

**Part 14 — Amendment of this Charter**

14.1 The Minister may, from time to time, by written notice to the Chair, amend this Charter. Amendments may include, but are not limited to, changes to:

(a) the name of the Committee;

(b) the functions of the Committee;

(c) the membership of the Committee, including the number of members and the categories of appointment;

(d) the term of appointment of members;

(e) the quorum for meetings;

(f) the reporting obligations of the Committee; and

(g) any other matter contained in this Charter.

14.2 Before making an amendment under clause 14.1, the Minister shall consult the Chair and shall have regard to any advice provided by the Committee in relation to the proposed amendment. The Minister is not bound by such advice.

14.3 Amendments made under this Part shall take effect on the date specified in the notice of amendment, or, if no date is specified, on the date the notice is issued.

14.4 The Chair shall ensure that all members are provided with a copy of any amendment as soon as practicable after the amendment is made, and the Secretariat shall maintain a consolidated version of the Charter incorporating all amendments in force from time to time.

14.5 Where an amendment affects the functions or operating procedures of the Committee, the Chair shall, where practicable, convene a special meeting of the Committee to consider the implications of the amendment and to make such adjustments to the Committee's working arrangements as may be necessary.

6.1 The Committee shall conduct its business in accordance with these Terms of Reference and with any directions given by the Minister from time to time.

6.2 Members shall act in good faith, and shall disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest in relation to any matter under consideration. A member with a conflict of interest shall not participate in the deliberation or decision on that matter, unless the Committee determines otherwise.

6.3 The Committee shall have regard to the need for transparency and accountability in its operations, and shall make publicly available, to the extent practicable, its reports and recommendations, subject to any applicable confidentiality requirements.

**7. ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT**

7.1 OPS shall provide secretariat and administrative support to the Committee, including the preparation of agendas, the circulation of papers, and the keeping of minutes.

7.2 The secretariat shall, in consultation with the Chair, prepare an agenda for each meeting and circulate it, together with any supporting papers, to members not less than seven days before the meeting, except in the case of an urgent meeting.

7.3 The Committee may adopt its own rules of procedure, not inconsistent with these Terms of Reference, for the conduct of its meetings and the discharge of its functions.

**8. REVIEW OF TERMS OF REFERENCE**

8.1 These Terms of Reference shall be reviewed by the Minister, in consultation with the Committee, no later than three years after the date of their commencement, and at intervals of no more than three years thereafter.

8.2 The Minister may amend these Terms of Reference at any time, after consultation with the Chair of the Committee.

**12. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

12.1 The Committee is committed to ensuring that its deliberations and recommendations are, and are seen to be, independent, impartial, and free from undue influence. Accordingly, members shall comply with the conflict of interest provisions set out in this clause and with any applicable requirements of the *Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013* (Cth) and the *Commonwealth Procurement Rules*.

12.2 For the purposes of this clause, a conflict of interest may be actual, potential, or perceived. A conflict arises where a member's personal, professional, financial, or other interests could be reasonably regarded as affecting, or appearing to affect, the member's ability to act in the best interests of the Committee and to discharge their duties objectively.

12.3 Each member shall, upon appointment and thereafter at the commencement of each financial year, complete and lodge with the Secretariat a declaration of interests in the form prescribed by the Chair. The declaration shall include:

(a) any financial interest, including shareholdings, directorships, partnerships, or other business interests, held by the member or by a member of their immediate family;

(b) any employment, consultancy, or other professional engagement undertaken by the member, whether paid or unpaid, that relates to the supply, manufacture, importation, or regulation of consumer products;

(c) any membership of, or advisory role with, any industry association, consumer organisation, professional body, or government committee whose activities may be relevant to the work of the Committee;

(d) any other matter that the member reasonably considers may give rise to a conflict of interest.

12.4 Members shall have a continuing obligation to disclose any new or changed interest as soon as practicable after the interest arises. Disclosure shall be made in writing to the Chair and to the Secretariat, and shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting of the Committee.

12.5 Where a matter before the Committee gives rise to a conflict of interest in relation to a member, that member shall:

(a) declare the nature of the conflict to the Committee prior to any discussion of the matter;

(b) not participate in any deliberation or decision in relation to the matter, unless the Committee, having considered the declaration, determines otherwise;

(c) absent themselves from the meeting during discussion and voting on the matter, unless the Committee determines otherwise; and

(d) not seek to influence, directly or indirectly, the deliberations or recommendations of the Committee in relation to the matter.

12.6 The Chair may, after consulting the member concerned, direct that a member with a conflict of interest take such further steps as are necessary to manage the conflict, including but not limited to restricting access to documents or excluding the member from certain parts of a meeting.

12.7 A member who is uncertain whether a conflict of interest exists in relation to a particular matter may raise the matter with the Chair, who shall determine the question in consultation with the member and, if necessary, with the Committee as a whole.

12.8 The register of interests shall be maintained by the Secretariat and shall be available for inspection by the Minister and, subject to any applicable privacy obligations, by other members of the Committee. The register shall not be made publicly available unless the Minister determines otherwise.

**CHARTER AND TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**AUSTRALIAN CONSUMER PRODUCT SAFETY ADVISORY COMMITTEE**

**Part 13 — Dissolution and Winding Up**

13.1 The Committee shall continue in existence until such time as the Minister, by written notice to the Chair, determines that the Committee is to be dissolved. The notice shall specify the date upon which the dissolution takes effect and any transitional arrangements that the Minister considers necessary or desirable.

13.2 Upon receipt of a notice of dissolution, the Chair shall, as soon as practicable, convene a meeting of the Committee for the purpose of:

(a) considering the notice and any transitional arrangements specified therein;

(b) preparing a final report to the Minister on the work of the Committee, including any outstanding recommendations or matters of concern;

(c) determining the arrangements for the custody and disposal of the records of the Committee, including minutes, reports, correspondence, and the register of interests; and

(d) considering any other matter arising from the dissolution.

13.3 The final report referred to in clause 13.2(b) shall be submitted to the Minister within 60 days of the date of dissolution, unless the Minister directs otherwise in writing.

13.4 The Secretariat shall, upon dissolution, transfer all records of the Committee to the Minister or to such other person or body as the Minister may direct. Records that are identified as having ongoing administrative value shall be retained in accordance with the Archives Act 1983 (Cth) and any other applicable record-keeping obligations.

13.5 Where a matter before the Committee is incomplete at the date of dissolution, the Chair shall include in the final report a summary of the matter, the progress made to date, and any recommendations for further action by the Minister or by any other body.

13.6 Nothing in this Part prevents the Minister from establishing a new committee with similar or related functions following the dissolution of the Committee, whether under the same name or under a different name.

**Part 14 — Amendment of this Charter**

14.1 The Minister may, from time to time, by written notice to the Chair, amend this Charter. Amendments may include, but are not limited to, changes to:

(a) the name of the Committee;

(b) the functions of the Committee;

(c) the membership of the Committee, including the number of members and the categories of appointment;

(d) the term of appointment of members;

(e) the quorum for meetings;

(f) the reporting obligations of the Committee; and

(g) any other matter contained in this Charter.

14.2 Before making an amendment under clause 14.1, the Minister shall consult the Chair and shall have regard to any advice provided by the Committee in relation to the proposed amendment. The Minister is not bound by such advice.

14.3 Amendments made under this Part shall take effect on the date specified in the notice of amendment, or, if no date is specified, on the date the notice is issued.

14.4 The Chair shall ensure that all members are provided with a copy of any amendment as soon as practicable after the amendment is made, and the Secretariat shall maintain a consolidated version of the Charter incorporating all amendments in force from time to time.

14.5 Where an amendment affects the functions or operating procedures of the Committee, the Chair shall, where practicable, convene a special meeting of the Committee to consider the implications of the amendment and to make such adjustments to the Committee's working arrangements as may be necessary.

Standards Register
Standards Australia – Consumer Product Safety Portfolio
Register current to 30 June 2017 (entries updated weekly; superseded versions retained for audit)

Notes on recent changes:

- AS 3720-2017 (Baby Walker Safety Standard 2017) was formally adopted as a mandatory standard on 2017-06-30 date. This version supersedes AS 3720-2015 in full. The standard applies to all wheeled, non-motorised baby walkers supplied in Australia from the adoption date. No transition period applies; the previous voluntary status ended on the adoption date.

- AS 2192-2017 (High Chairs) remains in development. The drafting committee met on 2017-05-08 to resolve comments on the restraint anchorage test. A further ballot is expected in August 2017. No adoption date has been set.

- AS 7002-2017 (Playpens) is in early drafting stage. The working group has circulated a preliminary scope document; industry feedback is due by 2017-07-21. This standard is not expected to reach publication until late 2018.

- AS 6200-2017 (Amendment 1 to Baby Bouncers & Rockers) was published on 2017-05-19 to correct a typographical error in Table 2 load figures. No other changes were made. The amendment is current and applies retrospectively to AS 6200-2015.

- AS 2088-2016 (Prams & Strollers) remains current. A routine five-year review is scheduled to commence in January 2018. The committee has noted that no critical safety issues have been reported since the 2016 revision.

Baby Walker Safety Standard 2017 mandatory_standard_adoption_date 2017-06-30 date. Record status: historical.

- AS 4410-2016 (Cots & Folding Cots) remains current. The standard was reissued in 2016 to incorporate new drop-side testing requirements. No further revisions are planned at this time.

- AS 5010-2017 (Change Tables) was updated on 2017-02-17 to clarify the edge-rounding measurement method. The update was initiated following a manufacturer inquiry about compliance interpretation. The change is considered minor; no product recalls have been linked to the previous version.

- AS 7001-2016 (Nursery Furniture – General Labelling) is current. The standard sets out labelling requirements for permanent warning labels on nursery furniture, including baby walkers. It is referenced by AS 3720-2017.

- Superseded versions remain on the register for audit and reference purposes. Suppliers may continue to use superseded versions only where the relevant mandatory standard or regulation explicitly permits, which is not the case for baby walkers.

- Standards with status “In development” are not yet published and have no legal effect. They are listed for transparency and to allow industry to track expected timelines.

- All version dates are publication dates. Adoption dates for mandatory standards are listed in the relevant OPS regulatory notice. For AS 3720-2017, the adoption date is 2017-06-30.

- Queries regarding this register should be directed to the Standards Development Coordinator, Consumer Product Safety Portfolio. The register is updated on a weekly basis; however, urgent amendments may be reflected within 48 hours of confirmation.

- The next full review of the register will be conducted on 2017-07-31 to confirm that all entries remain accurate following the adoption of AS 3720-2017.

End of register extract – page 1 of 1.

- The 2017 revision introduces a dynamic stability test that is more stringent than the static test used in the 2012 version. The committee also clarified the measurement of the gap between the walker frame and the seating platform, following a 2016 incident where a child’s finger became trapped. Note 8.1 – AS 3720-2017 (Baby Walkers, current)
This version was published on 2017-06-30 and is the only version that may
be used for products manufactured after 2018-01-01. The standard includes
a new requirement for a locking mechanism on folding walkers (clause 5.4)
and a revised test for dynamic stability (clause 6.2). The committee
expects that most manufacturers will transition to this version well
before the 2018 date, but the transition period was included to allow for
existing stock and tooling changes.

The 2017 version also introduced a requirement for a permanent warning
label on the product itself, in addition to the label on the packaging.
The label text is specified in AS 7001-2016 (see note 13.1 in the
previous extract). No further revisions are planned at this time.

Note 9.1 – AS 3720-2008 (Baby Walkers, superseded)
Superseded by AS 3720-2017 on 2017-06-30. The 2008 version was the first
to include a requirement for a locking mechanism on folding walkers; the
2003 version predates that requirement. The 2008 version may still be
used for products manufactured before 2018-01-01, provided the products
are not intended for export to markets that require the 2017 version.
No supplier has requested permission to use the 2008 version for ongoing
production beyond the transition date.

Note 10.1 – AS 3720-2003 (Baby Walkers, superseded)
Superseded by AS 3720-2008 on 2008-11-14. The 2003 version does not
include the locking-mechanism requirement. It may not be used for
products manufactured after 2009-01-01. The committee is not aware of
any supplier still using the 2003 version.

Note 11.1 – AS 4410-2016 (Cots & Folding Cots, current)
Reissued on 2016-05-11 to incorporate new drop-side testing requirements.
The previous version (AS 4410-2008) may still be used for products
manufactured before 2017-01-01. No further revisions are planned at this
time. The committee is, however, monitoring the outcomes of an ACCC
review of cot drop-side incidents reported between 2014 and 2016; if the
review recommends a change to the test method, a further revision may be
scheduled for 2018.

Note 12.1 – AS 5010-2017 (Change Tables, current)
Updated on 2017-02-17 to clarify the edge-rounding measurement method.
The update was initiated following a manufacturer inquiry about
compliance interpretation. The change is considered minor; no product
recalls have been linked to the previous version. The previous version
(AS 5010-2012) may still be used for products manufactured before
2017-08-01.

added after the 2017-09-14 review.
